description: The bar chart illustrates, for the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models,” the number of tasks in which one model is labeled as “better” (mBERT, XLM-R, or “same”) across several language-family groupings. The horizontal axis contains the categorical groups (left to right): IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, an unlabeled category shown as a gray-highlighted tick region, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic; the vertical axis is labeled “task count” and uses a linear scale from 0 to 40 with tick marks at 0, 10, 20, 30, and 40. Each category has three adjacent bars corresponding to the legend titled “better”: a light blue bar for mBERT, a darker blue bar for XLM-R, and a light green bar for same. Approximate bar heights by category are: IE-Baltic (mBERT ~0, XLM-R ~10, same ~7), IE-Germanic (mBERT ~4, XLM-R ~18, same ~22), IE-Indic (mBERT ~1, XLM-R ~5, same ~4), IE-Romance (mBERT ~4, XLM-R ~13, same ~30), the unlabeled gray-highlighted category (mBERT ~12, XLM-R ~39, same ~28), IE-other (mBERT ~1, XLM-R ~6, same ~8), Isolate (mBERT ~1, XLM-R ~5, same ~1), Semitic (mBERT ~0, XLM-R ~7, same ~1), and Uralic (mBERT ~1, XLM-R ~14, same ~5). The bars are grouped side-by-side within each category (not stacked), there is no indication that categories are sorted by value (they appear in a fixed family order), and the only visual emphasis is the gray shading behind the unlabeled category’s x-axis tick region; no bars are otherwise outlined or annotated.
